div.div: رَجَلٌ وَكَّاتٌ , mentioned by Kr; thought by ISd to be from وَكَتَ المَشْىَ; [and therefore to signify A man who walks, or goes, with short steps, but in a heavy and ugly manner]; because were it by the phrase mentioned by Kr [i. e. وَكّت فى سيره] it would be مُوَكِّتٌ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
